source_refs.note: Topic 9.8 with Fig. 9.18 (PDF 206-207, printed 203-204). The print spells 'positivity charged'.

blocks.text: The path of a charged particle is determined by the electric field in the region. The path is typically straight if the field is uniform and the charged particle is moving along the field. However, if a charged particle enters perpendicularly into the uniform field between oppositely charged parallel plates with a certain velocity (Fig. 9.18), it will not go straight. Its path will be parabolic, just like a projectile thrown horizontally in the gravitational field: the horizontal component of the velocity of the charged particle remains constant, whereas the vertical component is accelerated by the electric force.

blocks.alt: Two panels with plates + above and - below and magenta field lines pointing down. (a) A positive particle enters from the left and its dotted path curves down to the lower (-) plate. (b) A negative particle enters from the left and its dotted path curves up to the upper (+) plate.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.18 (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 9.18).

blocks.text: Figure 9.18 shows that a positively charged particle is attracted towards the negatively charged plate and thus undergoes deflection in that direction. On the other hand, a negatively charged particle is attracted towards the positively charged plate and is deflected in that direction.
